kill_fact: No kill. The two load-bearing bear mechanics verify exactly against the 30 June 2026 filing: clean trailing EBITDA is $4,342m (TTM EBITDA $8,664m less the $3,992m Prolec revaluation gain and $330m Proficy disposal gain booked in Q1 2026), net cash is $9,160m ($13,120m cash less $3,960m total debt), contract liabilities are $39,944m, and trailing-four-quarter working capital supplied $12,493m against trailing free cash flow of $12,439m — more than 100% of it. Management confirmed the mechanic verbatim on 22 July 2026 ("Working capital was a $6.4 billion cash benefit, driven primarily by higher down payments on increased orders and slot reservations at Power") and guided H2 2026 free cash flow far below H1 (roughly $10bn generated year to date against a $11.5-12.5bn full-year guide, i.e. $1.5-2.5bn in H2). But two numbers the thesis leans on are wrong, and one of them re-prices the base case.
corrections: (1) MATERIAL - the December 2025 investor-update anchor is overstated. bear_thesis cites "the company's own 2028 target of $11.2 billion" from "$56 billion of revenue at a 20% EBITDA margin." GE Vernova's own 9 December 2025 investor-update release states 2028 revenue of $52B at a 20% adjusted EBITDA margin - $10.4bn, not $11.2bn. This cuts two ways: on the multiple the thesis is too kind (EV of about $264bn is 25.4x the real 2028 plan, not 23.5x), but the base-case sum-of-the-parts was explicitly built as that plan "largely delivered but a notch light" at $10.0bn of 2028 EBITDA. The same 89.3% haircut applied to the correct $10.4bn plan gives $9.29bn, and carrying it pro-rata through the record's own schedule moves base fair value from $880 to about $810. Corrected in corrections_typed. (2) MATERIAL to the third leg - the backlog split is stale by a quarter. bear_thesis says "of 116 gigawatts under contract only about 44 are in formal backlog; the rest are slot reservation agreements" (implying ~72GW of SRAs). Those are the 31 March 2026 figures. On the 22 July 2026 call Ken Parks stated the 30 June position: "Backlog grew from 44 to 53 gigawatts, and SRAs increased from 56 to 63 gigawatts." So 53 of 116GW is firm backlog (46%, not 38%), and Q2 already converted 9GW of SRAs into orders - the opposite of the "slot reservations lapsing rather than converting" confirmation the thesis waits for. Management further guided that backlog gigawatts exceed SRA gigawatts by year-end. The qualitative point survives (54% of gigawatts under contract is still deposit-secured rather than contracted) but the specific ratio must be restated. (3) MINOR - the multi-year free-cash-flow target is misquoted: the 9 December 2025 release says "$22B+" cumulative over 2025 to 2028, not "at least $24 billion by 2028." On the correct four-year base, 2025 actual (about $3.9bn) plus the 2026 guide (about $12bn) already covers roughly 72% of the floor, leaving under $3bn a year implied for 2027-28 rather than the thesis's "$6 billion a year." The direction of the argument holds and is in fact understated - but note this is a floor set when 2026 was guided at $4.5-5.0bn of free cash flow, so treating it as a forecast is the softest link in the thesis. (4) MINOR - "roughly 92% above their 200-day average" is a conflation: at $1,019.74 the shares were about 22% above the then 200-day average of $836.50; 92% is the premium to the 52-week low of $530.16. The 200-day has since risen to $848.41 (11 August 2026), so risk_reward's claim that the attractive entry, the 200-day average and the parts calculation all coincide near $836 no longer holds - the corrected parts land near $810 while the moving average sits at $848. (5) MINOR - the "buying back stock at the top" characterisation is weaker than stated at the program level: on 22 July 2026 Parks disclosed cumulative repurchases of "approximately $7 billion ... representing 12.4 million shares at an average price of $560 per share" against a live price near $1,015. The H1 2026 tranche ($3.67bn per the cash-flow statement) was indeed bought near highs, but the aggregate program has been accretive, not a top-of-cycle error.

corrections_typed.basis: GE Vernova 2025 Investor Update release, 9 Dec 2025: 2028 target is $52B revenue at a 20% adjusted EBITDA margin = $10.4bn, not the $56B/$11.2bn used by the record. The base case is that plan 'largely delivered but a notch light' at $10.0bn, i.e. 89.3% of the anchor; 89.3% of the true $10.4bn is $9.29bn. Scaling the record's own schedule pro-rata: Power $5.20bn x21 = $109.3bn, Electrification $3.72bn x24 = $89.2bn, Wind $0.46bn x8 = $3.7bn, sum $202.2bn; plus $6.0bn SMR option, plus $9.2bn net cash (verified: $13,120m cash less $3,960m debt at 30 Jun 2026), less $1.2bn minority = $216.2bn equity / 268m shares = $807, rounded to $810.

evidence: GE Vernova Q2 2026 earnings call, 22 July 2026 (FMP transcript): Ken Parks - 'Backlog grew from 44 to 53 gigawatts, and SRAs increased from 56 to 63 gigawatts'; 'Working capital was a $6.4 billion cash benefit, driven primarily by higher down payments on increased orders and slot reservations at Power'; 'approximately $7 billion in share repurchases in total, representing 12.4 million shares at an average price of $560 per share'; FY26 free cash flow guidance raised to $11.5-12.5bn from $6.5-7.5bn; Scott Strazik - 'Year-to-date, we have generated approximately $10 billion in free cash flow.'

GE Vernova 2025 Investor Update press release, gevernova.com, 9 December 2025: 2028 outlook of '$52B' revenue and '20%' adjusted EBITDA margin (up from 14%), cumulative free cash flow of '$22B+' covering '2025 to 2028', backlog of approximately $200B by year-end 2028; 2026 guidance at that date was $41-42B revenue, 11-13% margin, $4.5-5.0B free cash flow.

GE Vernova Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, filed 22 July 2026 (via FMP statements): cash $13,120m vs total debt $3,960m = net cash $9,160m; contract liabilities $39,944m; gross margin $2,361m/$11,104m = 21.3% vs $1,846m/$9,111m = 20.3% in Q2 2025; TTM EBITDA $8,664m less the $3,992m Prolec revaluation and $330m Proficy gains booked in Q1 2026 = $4,342m clean; TTM change in working capital $12,493m vs TTM free cash flow $12,439m.

FMP quote, 11 August 2026: GEV $1,015.23, market capitalisation $270.4bn, 50-day average $1,021.20, 200-day average $848.41, 52-week range $530.16-$1,195.94 - enterprise value of about $262bn, i.e. 60x clean trailing EBITDA of $4.34bn and 25.4x the company's actual $10.4bn 2028 plan.
